scores.notes: The right roadside marker reads ROMAN, and pale unpainted margins remain along the bottom and corners; Saul and his companions otherwise react to bodiless radiance.
Daniel faces an empty fiery throne and wheels amid attendants; no human form occupies the light. The outer paper margin is visible, while the thin outline is not an ornamental frame.
Water flows from the rock and people and livestock drink, but Moses holds his staff upright on the ground and raises an empty hand rather than striking the rock.
Writing-like lines appear on loose courtroom papers and card markings at lower right; the enlarged Alice, tipping jury-box and tumbling animals otherwise fit the scene.
Peter is airborne beside the fishing boat clutching his coat, with a pointing disciple and a distant shore figure beside a fire; no clear requested fault is visible.
The central king stands in the temple court amid offerings and stoneworkers; visible hands, faces and architecture are coherent and no writing is evident.

Watson waits with a revolver on a crate and three companions across the dim vault. The polished faces suggest possible adaptation borrowing, but visual evidence alone is insufficient to establish that.
The father embraces and kisses his ragged son on the village road; the small background villagers do not become additional prominent subjects.
Goliath is arched backward with his face upward in an implausible airborne twist, rather than collapsing face-first; David's sling also appears still loaded.
Rows of glyph-like strokes cover the scroll and small initials appear at the lower left; the courtyard scribe and onlookers otherwise fit.
Fire falls onto two burning cities beneath dark clouds while small figures flee; there is no divine face or body and no explicit gore.
Dense rows of writing are visible on the foreground scroll; the scribe, lamp, wooden tablets and courtyard onlookers otherwise match.
Job braces one hand on the ash heap and looks into a bodiless storm; his low seated posture could be the start of rising, but the requested upright action is ambiguous.
Daniel stands below the rim while the king reaches toward him, but no attendants haul the rope and its loose path does not support a lift. White paper borders the scene.
Soldiers cast small lots and separate clothing below the cross; the crucifixion is restrained, with no readable placard or graphic wound.
Writing is visible on the newspaper, open book and bottle labels. Possible screen-adaptation borrowing in the character styling remains uncertain, but lettering is definite.
Letter-like marks run across Aaron's white lower hem; white paper remains around the illustration. Moses, Aaron, the pig and listeners are otherwise coherent.
Moses raises a hand beside Aaron while the pig roots before the listening crowd; the hem decoration reads as repeated ornament rather than clear inscription.
Naomi holds the infant while women gather closely at the stone house; no inscription, unrelated prominent figure or clear malformed limb is visible.
A bald prophet occupies the road at left as youths point and jeer from the gate; the townspeople and landscape support the requested episode.
Both helpers stand on Moses' right, leaving the staff-side raised arm unsupported rather than each supporting one side. White paper shows along the outer edges.
The father opens his arms before the son as servants bring a robe, ring and sandals; an unpainted wash margin is visible at the lower edge.
Ezekiel raises an arm toward scattered dry bones across the valley; there are no other living foreground figures or graphic remains.
The Levite holds a knife above the cloth-covered body in a lamplit room, with a donkey beyond the doorway; the scene remains restrained and without visible gore.
Disciples row and pour water over the gunwale beneath a torn sail; storm waves and nearby boats form one coherent scene.
Glyph-like vertical and curved marks run along the gold architectural frieze above the gate; paper remains visible at the margins. Peter's grip and the man's rising posture are clear.
One soldier drops lots while another gathers the blue garment below the crosses; the distant placard has no discernible inscription.
Waves break over the boat while disciples row and bail, with a torn sail overhead; no clear inscription or malformed limb is visible.
Radiance spreads over dark open water without any human-shaped deity; small areas of unpainted paper remain at the left and bottom edges.

The father gestures toward servants carrying a robe and sandals as the son leans toward him; the circular object carried by the servant is oversized for a finger ring, but the requested action remains clear.
The Caterpillar has a humanlike face and wears a bowler hat and buttoned waistcoat that the supplied text does not give it; Alice and the mushroom setting otherwise match.
Writing appears on the foreground correspondence and marks on the clock face; Holmes is alone opposite the empty chair. Possible adaptation-derived facial styling cannot be established conclusively.
The Gryphon and calf-headed Mock Turtle dance beside Alice on the shingle, with the permitted lobsters and turtles nearby; pale paper edges remain.

Open books and loose papers contain writing, and white margins surround the wash. Holmes appears to have an additional hand holding spectacles beside Watson's waist, beyond the doorknob hand and gripping hand.
The Hatter's pocket watch contains dial numerals and a signature-like inscription lies at lower right; the watercolor leaves white outer margins. The four tea-table subjects are present.
Loose papers and playing cards carry inscriptions; Alice remains an ordinary child-sized figure beside the court instead of showing the enormous growth central to the exchange.
One spear is airborne in front of David while a second spearhead and shaft are embedded directly behind his neck, combining the release and impact in an awkward duplicated trajectory.
Paul speaks with a raised hand to three seated listeners beside a doorway; the wash fades to white along the bottom and sides.
Alice listens as the wide-eyed Hatter speaks, the Hare raises a paw and the Dormouse sleeps; pale unpainted margins surround the tea scene.
Rows of writing are visible on loose papers at the lower right of the tipped jury-box; Alice's larger scale and the tumbling animal jurors are evident.
A luminous nonfigurative cloud rests above the central tabernacle while families remain beside their tents; unpainted paper shows at the outer corners and bottom.
Several dense columns of glyph-like writing and a heading occupy the open scroll; the seated scribe and courtyard listeners otherwise match.
The Caterpillar wears an added hat and waistcoat and has a distinctly human face; the supplied text permits human posture but does not supply that dress.
Samuel pours oil onto kneeling David while Jesse and three sons watch; the descending radiance has no human form, and white paper surrounds the wash.
Jesus raises a hand from the stern as the disciples look toward him and the water smooths in the distance; no clear requested fault is visible.
Paul stands centrally with an upraised hand among attentive courtyard listeners; scrolls remain rolled and no visible text or extra prominent subject appears.
Families, bundles and animals cross dry ground between two walls of water beside Moses; no human form appears in the sky or light.

A distinct translucent robed figure with a head and profile appears immediately left of Daniel, beyond the requested faceless glow. Daniel, the quiet lions and king otherwise match, and pale paper edges remain.
Samuel pours oil from a horn onto kneeling David as four relatives watch; the pale swirling light has no distinct face or body.
Families rest and tend small fires around the central tabernacle beneath a broad luminous cloud; the camp is stationary and no inscription is evident.
Hezekiah stands among priests, offerings and stoneworkers in the temple court; the tools and figures form a coherent single work scene.

Writing is visible on the left open book and papers on the central table and floor; the masked visitor pauses at the doorway before two seated men. Possible adaptation-derived styling remains inconclusive.
The priest releases pale feathers toward the ash pile beside the burning altar; the sanctuary courtyard and ritual are clear without visible gore.
Youths jeer and point at the bald prophet on the road outside the gate; white unpainted areas surround the watercolor, particularly along the bottom.
The stone stands beside an open cave while Darius presses a seal onto the ground in front; the den is not closed or secured by the sealing action.
The four travellers walk away from the burning house toward the viewer instead of hurrying toward it; three fire-engines work behind them. White paper remains along the lower edge.
Printed columns cover the tossed newspaper ball and scattered carriage papers; Holmes' throwing gesture and Watson seated opposite otherwise match.
Hezekiah gestures amid priests and temple workers, with offerings and bronze basins in the courtyard; a thin unpainted wash margin remains along the bottom.
The station-master carries a printed sheet, and the group strides away from the burning house rather than toward it; three fire-engines are visible behind.
Faint written lines appear on the papers lying on the table; Holmes points at the held paper while Lestrade leans in. Character styling raises an inconclusive adaptation-borrowing question.
An airborne spear points toward the upper right while a second short spearhead protrudes backward from the wall beside David, making the weapon trajectory contradictory.
Moses raises his rod beside a spurting rock while people and livestock approach the stream; the watercolor leaves unpainted outer margins.
Four distinct eye-covered winged creatures flank an empty radiant throne above the glassy sea; the human-faced winged creature is part of the requested four, not a figure seated as God.
Rephaiah gestures beside fresh wall courses while workers carry blocks and mortar and use a trowel; the rebuilding scene is coherent.
Peter steps from the boat onto the water toward Jesus while disciples watch by lamplight; the visible limbs and contact with the water are coherent.
Light floods the gateway as people lift hands and carry grain and jars toward stores; Wisdom is not given a separate face or figure.
Pinned wall notes, papers and the mantel clock contain writing or numerals; small white paper margins remain at the corners. The masked visitor and two seated men fit the requested encounter.
Written bills and notes cover the tabletop and numerals appear on the mantel clock; a small unpainted margin is visible at the bottom. Holmes and Lestrade focus on the paper.
Moses extends an arm over the opening sea while the people wait on the shore; the descending light is a shapeless column rather than a human figure.
The Hare gestures, the Dormouse sleeps and the wide-eyed Hatter addresses Alice at the tea-table; no legible or glyph-like hat label is visible.
Darius stamps a stone held above only part of the pit, leaving a large opening uncovered; the sealing action therefore cannot close the den. White paper appears at the bottom edge.
Hatherley points toward roses and a nearby window while Holmes watches; two separated burning building masses make the exact house layout ambiguous, although they may be wings of one property.
Jesus reclines on the stern cushion as frightened disciples reach toward him and bail water from the flooded boat; the storm and figures are coherent.
Chariots and horsemen pursue down the exposed seabed between high curling water walls; harnesses and densely grouped horses show no definite extra limb.
Suit-symbol inscriptions are visible on the background card gardeners; Alice whispers toward the floating cat head with the Queen close behind.

The pocket watch has numerals and cards bear suit and letter markings. Several left-side court officers have ordinary uniformed bodies rather than the required flat card bodies; the Hatter holds a visibly bitten cup.
David recoils beside a single spear embedded in the wall while Saul finishes the throw; smoke remains nonfigurative, and small pale paper edges are visible.
The lone man takes a step on the road below Jerusalem but remains markedly stooped, making restored strength uncertain; white paper shows along the left and bottom margins.
The father strides into an embrace with his travel-worn son on the village road; pale unpainted wash areas remain along the lower corners.
BULLION, BANK and other stencil-like text cover the crates; Holmes kneels with lens and lantern while Merryweather sits with his stick.
Rephaiah directs masons laying blocks while workers bring baskets and a cart; small white paper margins remain at the sides and bottom.
David crouches by the brook lifting a smooth stone, with an open stone-filled pouch, staff and loose sling; hands and legs are coherent.
The station-master holds a sheet with visible printed columns; Bradstreet looks toward the large smoke plume as two men stand at the train doorway.
The hovering seraphim expose their feet and several faces, with some showing only two or four wings rather than six arranged to cover face and feet. One also introduces the later coal-bearing action.
Small dial markings appear on the Hatter's pocket watch; white paper borders the wash. Alice addresses the Hare, protesting Hatter and sleepy Dormouse.
Goliath's torso bends forward but his head is twisted upside down with the face outward, producing an anatomically incoherent fall instead of a clear face-first collapse.
Alice brings the bottle to her mouth beside a table in the low hall; its hanging label is blank and the tiny low door gives a clear scale cue.
Daniel gestures openly before seated Belshazzar in the lamplit banquet hall; the wall behind the throne is blank and the surrounding guests are appropriate.
Chariots and mounted soldiers race through the exposed corridor between water walls; the close horse-and-rider overlaps do not reveal a definite malformed limb.

The priest drops feathers beside the altar, but two complete tabernacle structures appear at different scales, one in the left enclosure and one immediately behind him. A broad white margin surrounds the lower scene.
Alice speaks while the Hatter raises his cup, the Hare leans in and the Dormouse dozes among the cups; no clear inscription or malformed anatomy appears.
Fire rains from a bright cloud opening onto two cities as small figures flee; no face is formed in the sky, and unpainted paper shows at the sides and lower corners.
Daniel stands calmly among closed-mouthed lions beneath the king at the rim; the glow behind him has no distinct additional face or figure.
Adam lies with closed eyes and folded hands among quiet mourners in the courtyard; sheep and tools fit the setting, and the bottom wash fades to paper.
Peter jumps from the boat clutching his cloak toward Jesus on shore while a disciple points; unpainted margins remain around the sky and lower water.
Alice looks up at the grinning, clawed cat on a branch; the cat retains an animal body and the foliage scene has pale unpainted edge patches.
Naomi holds the swaddled infant while women gather at the doorway, one carrying the requested cloth bundle; pale unpainted patches remain along the lower edge.
Broad light enters from the upper left and spreads over dark, landless water; no face, body or human-shaped cloud is visible.

Suit glyphs and small rank-like marks appear on the background card figures; Alice whispers to the floating cat head with the Queen directly behind. Pale unpainted margins remain at the top and edges.
BULLION lettering is visible on the lower-right crate and faint marks on a left crate; white paper borders the wash. Holmes examines the floor while Merryweather sits nearby.
The priest drops feathers beside the altar, but a second complete tabernacle and enclosure appear at left while a large sanctuary stands immediately behind him, duplicating the setting.
Peter dives horizontally from the fishing boat toward the shore figure and fire, with the beloved disciple pointing; the coat is wrapped around him and no clear anatomical fault is visible.
